title: 17q21 genotype and PM2.5: how ORMDL3 and GSDMB regulation shifts asthma risk under air pollution exposure
question: Why does the same PM2.5 exposure level associate with different asthma risk in carriers of 17q21 risk haplotypes?
background: The chromosome 17q21 locus, which contains ORMDL3 and GSDMB, is the most consistently replicated common genetic signal for childhood-onset asthma. The asthma-risk haplotype does not change the protein sequence of these genes. It changes how much of them a cell makes. In airway epithelium, risk alleles raise ORMDL3 transcription and shift GSDMB toward pro-inflammatory splice forms. Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is one measurable part of the traffic and combustion pollution that Loudoun County residents encounter near arterials such as the Route 28 corridor. PM2.5 acts on the same airway epithelial cells that carry the 17q21 regulatory effect. This brief asks a narrow question: does 17q21 genotype change how the airway responds to a given amount of PM2.5, rather than adding a separate, independent increment of risk? The evidence for genotype-dependent expression at 17q21 is strong. The evidence that PM2.5 specifically interacts with that genotype is weaker, and it rests partly on inference from a better-studied exposure, tobacco smoke. Confidence in the specific interaction is therefore medium at best. Every statement here describes modeled, population-level associations. None of it estimates the risk of any individual.
evidence_summary: Established: Consortium genome-wide association studies identified 17q21 as the strongest common locus for childhood-onset asthma, first through ORMDL3 and later confirmed at scale [Moffatt et al., 2007; Moffatt et al., 2010].

Established: The 17q21 risk haplotype is a cis-regulatory signal. Verlaan and colleagues showed allele-specific chromatin remodeling, altered CTCF binding, and allele-specific expression of ORMDL3 and GSDMB across the region [Verlaan et al., 2009].

Established: In airway epithelial cells, raised ORMDL3 disturbs endoplasmic-reticulum calcium handling and facilitates the unfolded protein response [Cantero-Recasens et al., 2010], and it drives an ATF6 stress program together with metalloproteases and chemokines [Miller et al., 2012].

Established: Increased GSDMB expression is sufficient on its own to produce airway hyperresponsiveness and remodeling, including added smooth-muscle mass, in mice, and it does so without accompanying lung inflammation [Das et al., 2016].

Established for a different exposure: 17q21 risk alleles raise early-onset asthma risk mainly among children with early-life environmental tobacco smoke exposure, which is the clearest gene-by-environment result reported at this locus [Bouzigon et al., 2008].

Proposed: A specific 17q21-by-PM2.5 interaction is inferred rather than demonstrated. A genome-wide interaction study of air pollution and childhood asthma placed its interaction signals at ADCY2, B4GALT5, and DLG2, not at 17q21 [Gref et al., 2017].

Established: PM2.5 activates NF-κB in human airway epithelial cells through oxidative stress, which increases transcription of IL-33 and other cytokines that drive type 2 airway inflammation [Li et al., 2017].
mechanistic_chain: 1. PM2.5 from traffic and combustion deposits on the bronchial epithelium and generates reactive oxygen species at the cell surface. Molecular actors: particulate oxidants, epithelial membrane. Tissue: bronchial epithelium. Evidence class: functional [Li et al., 2017].

2. Oxidative stress activates the NF-κB pathway in bronchial epithelial cells, which raises transcription of IL-33 and other pro-inflammatory cytokines. Molecular actors: IKK complex, NF-κB, IL-33. Tissue: bronchial epithelium. Evidence class: functional [Li et al., 2017].

3. Independently of exposure, the 17q21 risk haplotype sets a higher baseline of ORMDL3 expression and shifts GSDMB toward pro-inflammatory isoforms through allele-specific regulation. Molecular actors: 17q21 cis-regulatory variants, ORMDL3, GSDMB. Tissue: bronchial epithelium. Evidence class: eQTL and functional [Verlaan et al., 2009; Moffatt et al., 2010].

4. Elevated ORMDL3 disturbs endoplasmic-reticulum calcium handling and activates the ATF6 arm of the unfolded protein response, holding the epithelium in a state of low-grade stress. Molecular actors: ORMDL3, SERCA, ATF6. Tissue: bronchial epithelium. Evidence class: functional [Cantero-Recasens et al., 2010; Miller et al., 2012].

5. Elevated GSDMB lowers the threshold for epithelial pyroptosis and, on its own, increases airway smooth-muscle mass and responsiveness. Molecular actors: GSDMB N-terminal pore domain, airway smooth muscle. Tissue: bronchial epithelium and airway smooth muscle. Evidence class: functional [Das et al., 2016].

6. IL-33 released from stressed epithelium engages the ST2 receptor on group 2 innate lymphoid cells, which secrete IL-5 and IL-13 and recruit eosinophils. Molecular actors: IL-33, ST2, ILC2s. Tissue: airway wall. Evidence class: functional [Cayrol & Girard, 2018].

7. A genetically primed epithelium, already carrying more ER stress from ORMDL3 and a lower pyroptosis threshold from GSDMB, is proposed to mount a larger NF-κB and IL-33 response to a given PM2.5 dose than a non-primed epithelium. Evidence class: inferred.

8. Across a population, this predicts a steeper slope of asthma risk against PM2.5 exposure in carriers of the 17q21 risk haplotype than in non-carriers. This is the testable prediction of the model, not an established measurement. Evidence class: inferred.
tissue_specificity: The two arms of this mechanism meet in the bronchial epithelium. PM2.5 deposition, oxidative stress, NF-κB activation, and IL-33 release all occur in airway epithelial cells, and these are the same cells in which the 17q21 regulatory variants act. ORMDL3 and GSDMB are both expressed in human bronchial epithelium in GTEx v8 data, and their asthma-risk alleles alter expression in that tissue [Verlaan et al., 2009; Miller et al., 2012]. IL33 is expressed in lung and bronchial epithelium and behaves as a barrier-restricted alarmin. Airway smooth muscle is the second relevant tissue. Raised GSDMB by itself increased smooth-muscle mass and airway responsiveness in mice without inflammation, which places part of the remodeling phenotype downstream of genotype rather than downstream of the inflammatory response [Das et al., 2016]. Allele-specific effects reported in lymphoblastoid cell lines are not treated here as airway evidence.
counterarguments: The gene-by-environment interaction at 17q21 is not uniform across cohorts or exposure proxies. The strongest and most replicated interaction is with tobacco smoke [Bouzigon et al., 2008]. A genome-wide interaction analysis of air pollution did not place its top signals at 17q21 [Gref et al., 2017], so a clean ORMDL3 or GSDMB by PM2.5 interaction should be read as a hypothesis rather than a finding.

PM2.5 is a mixture, not a single agent. Monitor-based annual means are a coarse stand-in for what a given person actually breathes, and they move together with co-exposures such as ultrafine particles, black carbon, and traffic noise. An association assigned to PM2.5 may belong partly to those correlates.

The genetic findings at 17q21 come mostly from European-ancestry samples. Effect sizes are smaller and less consistent in African American and Latino cohorts, and multi-ancestry work is still catching up [Torgerson et al., 2011]. The 17q21 risk haplotype is common in European ancestry, near 50 percent, and less common in African ancestry, near 20 percent, and its regulatory effect can differ by ancestry. Loudoun County has large South Asian, Black, and Hispanic and Latino populations, so applying this model to the county without ancestry-specific data would overreach.

Exposure here is assigned by place, not by person. Linking tract-level or monitor-level pollution to asthma rates invites the ecological fallacy: a correlation measured across places does not establish that the same relationship holds within individuals.
validation_criteria: Air-liquid interface cultures of primary human bronchial epithelial cells from 17q21 risk-allele and non-risk donors, exposed to controlled PM2.5. Measure IL-33 release, ATF6 and unfolded-protein-response markers, and NF-κB activation. A real interaction predicts a larger increase in risk-allele cells at the same dose, tested with a formal genotype-by-dose term.

A multi-ancestry gene-environment study that pairs genome-wide genotypes with modeled residential PM2.5 and tests whether any 17q21 interaction holds across ancestry groups or instead reflects European-specific linkage. If the model is correct, the interaction should hold in the same direction after accounting for linkage differences.

A birth cohort along the Route 28 and Dulles corridor with spatiotemporal PM2.5 estimates linked to home and school addresses, testing whether the slope of asthma incidence against PM2.5 is steeper in 17q21 carriers after adjustment for socioeconomic confounders. A null interaction would weaken the hypothesis.
